newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt dragged lower by U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: German debt dragged lower by U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: German Bunds and futures slipped down in late European trade, unwilling to make a convincing break higher while U.S. Treausuries remained soft.
"The market has come off a bit this afternoon," said one Frankfurt-based trader.
"We saw some quite heavy selling in the three-year area of the cash market, but overall the Bunds still have a fairly positive note," she added.
By 1427 GMT, the DTB June Bund future was three basis points down on the day at 100.83, well off its earlier high at 101.05 when the contract took out resistance at 101.01.
"We pushed gradually higher this morning, and considering that there was some fairly good selling this afternoon at three years, we haven't done too badly," the trader said.
In the cash market, the 10-year benchmark Bund was quoted at 101.06 by 1432 GMT for a yield of 5.844 percent. Three-year paper was at 106.60 for a bid yield of 4.022 percent.
The 10-year Bund/T-note yield gap was at 117 basis points.
Analysts said that with Treasuries heading south in early business, players on the German market were wary, happier to let prices trade a range rather than trying to push through resistance levels.

Another trader based in Frankfurt confirmed that there had been some selling in the three-year area of the curve, but said these players were not switching out of the German market, but rather lengthening their portfolio duration.
Volumes were pretty low, he said.
"The cash market has been very quiet for days now," he said. "Retail clients are unwilling to come in while the market is so lacking in direction."
With little on the horizon to offer direction for Bunds, traders said the June future was likely to remain in a 100.70 to 101.10 trading range ahead of the weekend.
That range has fenced the contract in for the last five trading sessions.
Beyond the weekend, the next focal point for the market would be Tuesday's release of the U.S. first quarter 1997 employment cost index, analysts said.
